description: Rowan, who repairs bicycles as a side business, needs care for his dog while he is away and must decide whether to accept Felix's offer of dog-sitting in exchange for a bicycle tune-up. Rowan will make the final call and settle the care, repair, payment comparison, and key-handoff terms.

shared_context.S1: Rowan will be away from July 6 through July 13 and needs someone to stay with his dog during that trip.
shared_context.S2: Rowan repairs bicycles and is considering exchanging that work for dog care rather than arranging an ordinary paid booking.
shared_context.S3: Felix has offered to care for the dog, and everyone is meeting at Rowan's home to settle the arrangement.
shared_context.S4: Rowan's usual practice for an informal swap is to ask each person present for relevant practical details before agreeing to terms.
shared_context.S5: Rowan makes the final decision about whether the swap goes ahead and what the verbal terms will be.
shared_context.S6: For Rowan's usual swap ledger, each person must formally disclose any exact offer, requirement, or logistical fact they know before Rowan finalizes the arrangement, and Rowan records every disclosed material fact that changes a settlement term.
shared_context.S7: When a disclosed fact changes a settlement term, Rowan's normal recordkeeping practice is to cite that fact in the final explanation of the term, whether the swap is accepted or declined.
shared_context.S8: If someone's response is unclear or does not come through properly, Rowan's normal practice is to ask that person to restate the relevant details before he finalizes the ledger.

PF1.text: Felix's offer is seven overnight stays from July 6 through July 13 in exchange for a full touring-bike tune-up, including a new chain and rear brake cable, with the repaired bike returned by July 20.

PF2.text: Mara can provide the same July 6 through July 13 dog care for exactly $280, giving Rowan a concrete paid alternative to Felix's swap.

PF3.text: Dr. Chen reviewed the dog's current care sheet and knows the dog must receive insulin at exactly 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. each day and must not be taken off leash.

PF4.text: Lena knows the building does not allow a keybox; Felix must receive the apartment key in person on July 5 and return it to Lena in person on July 13.

acceptance_conditions: The service swap must be accepted.
Felix must provide seven overnight stays from July 6 through July 13.
Rowan must provide a full touring-bike tune-up including a new chain and rear brake cable, with the bike returned by July 20.
The $280 paid alternative must be recorded before selecting the swap.
The dog must receive insulin at exactly 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. each day.
The dog must not be taken off leash.
The apartment key must be handed over in person on July 5 and returned in person on July 13.
The insulin schedule must be justified using the veterinary-care fact that was spoken aloud.
Felix's exact offer terms must be formally disclosed and cited in the final explanation of the swap terms.
Mara's exact $280 alternative must be formally disclosed and cited in the final explanation of the payment comparison.

content_checks.C3: decisions['bike_service'] == 'full touring-bike tune-up' and (decisions['bike_parts_replaced'] == ['chain', 'rear brake cable'] or decisions['bike_parts_replaced'] == ['new chain', 'rear brake cable'] or decisions['bike_parts_replaced'] == ['new chain', 'new rear brake cable']) and decisions['bike_return_date'] == 'July 20'
content_checks.C5: decisions['insulin_morning_time'] == '7:00 a.m.' and decisions['insulin_evening_time'] == '7:00 p.m.' and decisions['off_leash_allowed'] == False
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'dog_care' and c['target'] == 'Felix' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'bike_repair' and (c['target'] == 'Felix' or c['target'] == 'Rowan') for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Felix's exact offer changes the settlement to July 6-July 13 care, a full touring-bike tune-up with a new chain and rear brake cable, and a July 20 return date.
Mara's exact $280 alternative supplies the concrete comparison that supports accepting Felix's swap and requires recording exactly $280 before choosing it.
The veterinary-care information changes the dog-care terms to insulin at exactly 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. with no off-leash walks, and requires Rowan to cite that schedule's source.
The building's keybox restriction changes the access arrangement to an in-person handoff on July 5 and an in-person return on July 13.
